output_raw: The Prime Minister of India thanked the Secretary-General for his clear account of the crisis in Ukraine. She also thanked President Zelenskyy for his statement emphasizing the unfailing support of Ukraine in its response to Russian aggression. However, India calls for a more balanced reporting on the impact of the war. India has taken and is continuing to take all possible measures, including the latest restrictions on the export of jets and engines, to meet the needs of Ukraine while ensuring caution and responsibility. But we receive many reports of the impact of arms transfers to Ukraine exacerbating the intensity and pace of fighting. The recent escalation in attacks on Ukrainian cities cannot be wholly dismissed as a result of Russian planning and strategy alone. What we need is to stop the bleeding and save lives — Ukrainian, Russian and those of civilians around the world. That is why India is continuing to engage rigorously with all parties, in addition to leading the Initiative for Responsible Nation-States (INNS). The Observer Status to the INNS will be announced soon. Let us move purposefully towards a peaceful resolution to this issue.<|im_end|>

I thank the Secretary-General for his clear and balanced account of the Russian invasion of Ukraine and the suffering it has caused. The United Kingdom condemns ruthlessly the Russian attack on Ukraine, which is an unlawful use of force and a violation of the Charter of the United Nations. We stand with Ukraine in our moral and political support. But we also emphasize that our approach is holistic, as is clear in recent British policy statements. While we have been unswerving in our condemnation of Russia’s invasion, we have also been clear that we want a sustainable peace for Ukraine and the region. Therefore, we have engaged constructively with all parties to the conflict, including Russia, to keep open all paths to peace. I recently met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Russian President Vladimir Putin, and we both emphasized our respective positions on the conditions for ending the war. But there is now an urgent need to prevent further loss of life and to stop the escalation of the conflict. We recently reported concerns about the risk of further escalation, in particular around the recent military moves near Ukraine’s northern border and the activities of proxy forces in Ukraine’s east. We warned of that risk clearly to both Russia and Ukraine. We regret the decision by Russia to launch attacks against UK defence providers in Ukraine, which was a terrible mistake that increased the danger of escalation. We condemned those attacks strongly and took targeted measures in response. But we urge caution and restraint from all sides. There should be no attacks on Ukrainian defence providers from either side. We report concern about recent increases in cross-border fire in Ukraine, with more Ukrainian forces reporting attacks from Russian sources around the Dnipro and Dnieper regions. There have also been several incidents involving third parties near the border between Ukraine and Russia. All too often, groups affiliated with both Russian and Ukrainian forces have been among those suffering in the crossfire. We call for maximum caution and restraint to prevent further tragedy and the further escalation of the conflict. The long-term solution to the conflict must be based on lasting peace. The UK has been clear that any peaceful resolution to the war must be built on respect for Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, including its international borders. That is a necessary precondition for a durable peace. But we again emphasize that there are multiple ways to end the war and bring about peace. There needs to be a clear path to security for Ukraine.

I want to thank you for your statement. The United States strongly condemns the Russian Federation’s invasion of Ukraine, an act of aggressive war that rejects core principles of international order. The United States has provided Ukraine with vital assistance to defend itself against Russia’s attack. We are making all necessary extensions to military aid packages and have announced a range of new supports, including $1.6 billion in emergency assistance last week to help Ukraine maintain its defense and protect its civilians. Today, I announced $1 billion to support Ukraine’s long-term security needs, including training and equipping Ukrainian forces, as well as support for Ukraine’s energy security and economic resilience. We are also leading an international coalition to raise additional resources to support Ukraine over the long term. It is critical that Ukraine has the resources it needs to defend itself against Russia’s aggression. The Secretary-General’s briefing highlighted the suffering of civilians in Ukraine and around the world. We deeply regret the many civilians killed or injured, especially children and women. We regret the numbers of displaced people around the world, including many Europeans, as a result of the war in Ukraine. And we regret the way the war is impacting our common challenges, from inflation to energy prices to supply chains. We recently emphasized that we cannot ignore the threat of Russian weapons to European nations or the further expansion of rogue states and their proxies around the world. With Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, there is a clear and increasing risk of weapons to weapons escalation, as we saw with the recent attacks on Ukrainian defense providers by Russian forces and your report’s account of Russian troops attacking Ukrainian forces near the border between Ukraine and Russia. We reiterate our call for maximum caution and restraint to help prevent further escalation and suffering. We also regret the recent attacks on dual-nationality engineers from the United Kingdom and the United States near Bakhmut, Ukraine, a stark reminder of the dangers of war and the risks of escalation. We stand in unequivocal support of Ukraine’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and independence, in line with the Charter of the United Nations. But we also emphasize that we support a peaceful resolution to the war in Ukraine. There needs to be a path forward that is secure for Ukraine and that addresses the concerns of all parties to the conflict. The United States is engaged in peace efforts with both Russia and Ukraine and will continue to work to keep all paths to peace open.<|im_end|>
